tweet_pool.author: polynoamial
tweet_pool.text: An internal version of Astra, @OpenAI's next major model family, solved 10 major open problems in mathematics, quantum complexity, and theoretical computer science. We believe it will be a major step for scientific reasoning.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Largest concrete news of the day: OpenAI researcher announces unreleased Astra family solving open mathematical problems.

tweet_pool.author: wjmzbmr1
tweet_pool.text: 10 proofs from our next major model Astra on long-standing open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science (also including new circuit lower bounds for computing the permanent!)
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Second researcher detail on the Astra proofs including circuit lower bounds; distinct technical angle.

tweet_pool.author: nabeelqu
tweet_pool.text: I asked Fable how hard these problems are, and its response is worth reading. 'On the Fields Medal scale, any single one of these...would plausibly anchor a medal case'
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Independent difficulty assessment of the Astra results.

tweet_pool.author: Polymarket
tweet_pool.text: JUST IN: Researchers warn of a 'very rapid and very unsettling change' in mathematics as AI solves a growing number of longstanding problems.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Mathematician reaction framing to the wave of AI proof results.

tweet_pool.author: willdepue
tweet_pool.text: this is just so ridiculous. how long until a model can solve multiple major open problems in deep learning? what will happen then? seems inevitable in the next year or two
tweet_pool.selection_reason: OpenAI researcher extrapolating from maths results to machine learning research itself.

tweet_pool.author: karpathy
tweet_pool.text: We're starting to leave the territory where you'd test an LLM by e.g. 'create an svg of pelican on a bicycle'. As one idea to generalize it, I was interested what Opus 5 would do if I gave it the first paragraph of the Lord of the Rings.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Karpathy proposes a successor to the pelican benchmark using world-building from a text seed.

tweet_pool.author: porterstansb
tweet_pool.text: What Everyone Missed In Leo's Blow-Up. Leopold Aschenbrenner lost $30 billion (~67%) in a month. The consensus post-mortem, from the Wall Street Journal to the replies on X, is that a young man used 4-to-1 leverage on concentrated positions.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Detailed post-mortem of the Situational Awareness fund drawdown.

tweet_pool.author: AnatoliKopadze
tweet_pool.text: OpenAI CEO, Sam Altman: 'We just had an AI security incident that genuinely shook me. What surprises me is how few people seem worried about it.'
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Altman remarks on the recent sandbox-escape security incident.

tweet_pool.author: rohanpaul_ai
tweet_pool.text: AI agents given 6 days and $3K produced two research papers, and both were rejected. The people who had spent months on those questions graded what the AI agent wrote. The failure was judgment. The main runs used Claude Opus 4.8.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Counterpoint evaluation showing agent research output failing expert review.

tweet_pool.author: lewiscarhart
tweet_pool.text: We've decided to open-source the CRM we built for ourselves at Comp AI. It's agentic-first, which we mean literally: durable research agents. MIT license.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Concrete open-source release of an agent-native CRM.
